lines.text: Most companies have automated tasks.
But the expensive part happens between the tasks: a claim waiting on an approval,
an invoice waiting on a person, an agent handing off to a robot.
UiPath Maestro is built for that in-between.
In five minutes: two products, one engine, and how to choose.
UiPath Maestro has two products on one engine: durable, stateful execution built for the enterprise.
Maestro Automate is for short-running workflows of AI agents and APIs, finished within minutes or hours.
Maestro Orchestrate is for long-running business processes that coordinate agents, robots, and people.
Start with Orchestrate.
It coordinates AI agents, robots, and people across the systems you already run.
An instance can hold its state for hours, days, or weeks while it waits on a person, a system, or an event.
There is no cap on duration or concurrency, and it survives failures and redeployments.
You pick the canvas: [BPMN|Bee Pee Em En], Case, or Flow.
The canvas changes how you build. What runs underneath stays the same.
Maestro [BPMN|Bee Pee Em En] is for a process that business and IT both sign off on.
You model it in [BPMN|Bee Pee Em En,] 2.0, extended with UiPath tasks for robots, agents, and sub-processes.
Business rules live in [DMN|D M N] decision tables, versioned alongside the model.
And the diagram you sign off on is the one that runs. No re-implementation step.
Maestro Case is for work that doesn't follow a straight line: claims, loans, disputes, and referrals.
You model stages, milestones, and [SLAs|S L As] up front.
Then events, AI decisions, and human judgment decide the order.
A Case Manager agent governs the lifecycle, Stage Manager agents drive each phase,
and people stay in the loop where judgment matters.
Maestro Flow is the developer-first canvas.
Agents, APIs, data, documents, and human steps are all nodes on one canvas.
Describe what you want and a coding agent builds it, or refine it visually.
The same flow file opens in the cloud canvas or in [VS Code|V S Code], and lives in Git.
Whichever canvas you pick, you stay in control of live instances.
Retry, cancel, pause, resume, migrate, or go to a step, one at a time or in bulk.
Every step and variable is recorded,
and policy, access control, and a tamper-evident audit trail come from the UiPath Platform.
Now Maestro Automate.
An event comes in, agents reason, APIs act, and the workflow finishes within minutes or hours.
Take order intake: an order arrives by webhook, an agent validates it,
checks stock and credit over API, and creates the order in the ERP.
Build it in your editor with a coding agent like Claude Code, Codex, or Copilot.
Debug it with probes and breakpoints, and evaluate it before it goes live.
Your existing robots, API workflows, and agents are called as nodes, not rebuilt.
So which one?
Choose Automate when the workflow is short-running and the builder wants speed.
Choose Orchestrate when the process runs long and carries the business.
It is not either-or. A workflow that outgrows Automate converts to Orchestrate:
same canvas, same file, nothing to rebuild.
To start, create a project under Business Orchestration in [VS Code|V S Code] or Studio Web, and pick [BPMN|Bee Pee Em En], Case, or Flow.
Orchestrate the whole process, not just the tasks.
